Breakdown.IsPerturbation.text: The square-integrable transport field combines the time derivative, dilation and half the velocity before subtracting the Laplacian. The second spatial derivatives are weak derivatives.

Breakdown.ExtendedCertificateData.target.text: The pin targets are prescribed for the full profile. Subtracting the approximate profile’s pins gives the correction targets used in the bordered problem.

Breakdown.Cert.XX.text: The complete iteration space controls the two spatial derivative norms. Each bordered solve supplies the additional time equation required for membership in $D_S$.

Breakdown.Cert.extendedHeldContractsHold.text: Condition (7.26) controls the supremum part of the difference distance. The paper’s simultaneous Schauder–Tychonoff proof does not use this condition.

Breakdown.Cert.extendedDataContinuityHol.text: The continuity argument uses residual pairings with compact solenoidal tests. The chosen residual need not vary continuously in the H norm.

Breakdown.Cert.extendedSupBoundHolds_of.text: The shorter period is required only for scalar enstrophy. The forcing representative can have period one, which is sufficient for the full-period averaging argument.

Breakdown.Cert.readingEnergyHolds_of.text: The physical energy uses the Frobenius square of the gradient and the trace of a weak Hessian. Their agreement with the derivative-space norm uses the closed spatial derivative relation.

Breakdown.extended_certificate_orbit_pro.text: The public conclusion retains only weak-profile existence. Carrying the selected parameter, correction, pins and joint bound through smoothing requires the separately described same-witness construction.

Breakdown.Cert.HH.text: The paper’s H contains all periodic square-integrable physical forcing fields. The formal forcing space contains their solenoidal Fourier projections, so the two spaces agree only after projection and physical interpretation.

Breakdown.Cert.Internal.BorderedInvertib.text: The formal result inverts a bordered identity-plus-compact operator on a complete normed space, assuming invariance and injectivity. The account applies this operator theorem to $T_S$, convection, actuators and pins after proving those hypotheses.

Breakdown.Cert.Internal.HeldMetric.isClo.text: Every essential-supremum sublevel is closed under L² convergence. This is the lower-semicontinuity fact used to keep the held gradient bound under limits.
The essential gradient-supremum constraint B(v)≤M is closed in the spatial derivative space, exactly the constraint used in the held-set argument.

Breakdown.Cert.Internal.ProductBound.wea.text: Two weak gradients of the same velocity agree almost everywhere. This permits derivative identities to be preserved when the physical representative is changed.

Breakdown.Cert.Internal.ReadingEnergy.en.text: For a bounded positive weight, the physical integral of |Δv|²+w|∇v|F² equals the energy in the spatial derivative representation. The equality retains the full weight and the Frobenius gradient norm.

Breakdown.Cert.Internal.ReadingEnergy.pi.text: The physical pin ∫∇v:Ξ_i over one period equals the corresponding pairing of the gradient representation. This is the pin identity needed when replacing representatives.

Breakdown.Cert.Internal.ReadingExists.is.text: Almost-everywhere equality of the velocity and gradient representatives preserves the weak-gradient relation. Applying this to gradient columns also permits transport of a weak Hessian.

Breakdown.Cert.TimeCircle.text: Time is taken modulo one, giving the period-one circle ℝ/ℤ.

Breakdown.Cert.XBar.text: The spatial derivative space consists of a homogeneous first-derivative symbol paired with its negative Laplacian, with both components square integrable.

Breakdown.Cert.XX.text: The complete ambient space contains period-one $L^2$ fields with a square-integrable Laplacian. The paper’s $D_S$ additionally requires the combined time-and-dilation equation; that extra condition is imposed by the inverse, not by the ambient iteration space.

Breakdown.Cert.contractionFixedPointHold.text: The fixed-point theorem works in any complete normed ambient space with a closed set and a distance that controls its norm, satisfies the triangle inequality and passes bounds to limits. The account applies it to the particular held distance.

Breakdown.Cert.exists_gradInvSpec.text: The construction gives the homogeneous gradient through a bounded heat-dilation integral. A separate extension into the spatial derivative space and a test-equation argument yield the physical inverse of $T_S$.

Breakdown.Cert.exists_projSpec.text: The result constructs the spatial Leray projection. Lemma II.2’s equivalence with annihilation of all space-time solenoidal tests also uses the separate pairing and separation results.

Breakdown.Cert.extendedAdjointEnclosureH.text: The result bounds the adjoint coordinates of the held correction after multiplier weight one and reference Wᵃ have been adopted. The account restores the original ω and adds the affine offset to obtain inclusion of the raw parameter update.

Breakdown.Cert.extendedAdjointPairingHol.text: The representative-independent adjoint condition at zero perturbation forces ψ to be solenoidal in H. Consequently its pairing with any admissible F agrees with the pairing of their solenoidal projections.

Breakdown.Cert.extendedAtProfileHolds.text: The theorem proves that replacing the reference by Wᵃ preserves the certificate after dividing c₁, c₂ and c₀ by 1−ϑ and row weights by (1−ϑ)². The account writes the equivalent physical absorption inequality before this rescaling.

Breakdown.Cert.extendedBorderedInvertibl.text: The formal result solves the projected bordered equation after setting the reference to Wᵃ and the multiplier weight to one. The physical-domain bijection in Proposition II.9 also uses the representation of the free inverse and the forcing test identities.

Breakdown.Cert.extendedCoerciveBorderedH.text: The bound is stated for the normalised certificate and the physical representative of the bordered output. The account retains the original multiplier weight and the factor 1−ϑ, recovered by undoing the normalisations.

Breakdown.Cert.extendedConvectionCompact.text: The theorem proves compactness of projected convection composed with the free inverse using local velocity and gradient compactness plus small exterior contributions. The account gives a physical weakly-null-sequence proof and obtains gradient convergence by cutoff integration by parts.

Breakdown.Cert.extendedConvectionHolds_o.text: The formal conclusion supplies a bounded projected convection operator for each parameter and identifies its physical test pairings. The account’s statement also includes a uniform parameter bound, invariance and compactness, which require additional results.

Breakdown.Cert.extendedDataContinuityHol.text: The result proves continuity of the correction pin target and of every residual pairing with a compact solenoidal test. It imposes no H norm-continuity requirement on the residual representative.

Breakdown.Cert.extendedExistsZeroHeldHol.text: The theorem selects a zero-force parameter from unique held solutions, multiplier continuity and coordinate enclosures after both normalisations. The paper selects a parameter and proposed quadratic forcing simultaneously by Schauder–Tychonoff.

Breakdown.Cert.extendedFrozenBridgeHolds.text: The bridge applies the reference frozen-form inequality and form-transfer error to almost every slice of a free solution. The paper first imposes an every-time inequality for all admissible spatial fields; the bridge is its application to the constructed solution.

Breakdown.Cert.extendedHeldContractsHold.text: The proof uses (7.26) to control the supremum part of the difference distance and obtains contraction factor 2cLc_wM<1. The paper’s simultaneous Schauder–Tychonoff construction leaves (7.26) unused.

Breakdown.Cert.extendedHeldExistsUniqueH.text: The formal construction gives a unique held solution at every fixed parameter after normalisation. The paper’s Proposition 7.10 obtains existence while choosing a parameter and forcing simultaneously; its statement does not assert fixed-parameter uniqueness.

Breakdown.Cert.extendedHeldLimitHolds_of.text: The theorem extracts a limiting nonlinear held solution as its parameter varies, preserving the equation, pins and both bounds. The paper’s continuity step instead passes to limits of bordered linear solves indexed by an independent quadratic forcing.

Breakdown.Cert.extendedHeldMapsToHolds_o.text: The result preserves the held joint radius and gradient-supremum bound for the nonlinear step at a fixed parameter after normalisation. The paper’s self-map has an additional parameter and independent quadratic-forcing component.

Breakdown.Cert.extendedHeldMetricHolds_o.text: The result proves closedness of the held set, positive control of the ambient norm, the triangle inequality and stability of distance bounds under ambient limits. These are the properties used in the account’s completeness and contraction argument.

Breakdown.Cert.extendedHeldNonzeroHolds_.text: The theorem rules out almost-everywhere vanishing of Wᵃ+v for every held correction by the strict separation inequality. Force cancellation is unnecessary for this nonvanishing argument.

Breakdown.Cert.extendedHeldWeakEquationH.text: The theorem proves integrability and vanishing of the tested weak similarity expression for the chosen sum after exact force cancellation. The account’s Proposition II.16 additionally asserts nonvanishing and continuity in X, supplied by other steps.

Breakdown.Cert.extendedInvarianceHolds_o.text: The result proves invariance of projected convection, quadratic forcing, actuators and the residual under each prescribed space-time symmetry. It does not require the chosen unprojected residual to be invariant.

Breakdown.Cert.extendedMultiplierContinu.text: The public conclusion gives continuity of the total coefficient βᵃ+β, after compactness and uniqueness of held solutions. The account states continuity of β separately; subtracting the given continuous βᵃ recovers that assertion.

Breakdown.Cert.extendedStiffEnclosureHol.text: The theorem bounds the held multiplier’s complementary-coordinate contribution by 2εa*/ω after normalisation. The full weighted-ball inclusion also adds the affine offset and uses its inclusion inequality.

Breakdown.Cert.extendedSupBoundHolds_of.text: The theorem bounds the essential gradient supremum using the projected bordered forcing and actual period S(α)/m. The account gives the corresponding every-time bound for a continuous physical representative and any admissible right-side representative.

Breakdown.Cert.extendedUnitWeightHolds.text: Dividing actuators and V by ω while multiplying the coefficient vectors by ω produces another certificate with multiplier weight one. The physical force, parameter update, period, profile and pin targets are preserved.

Breakdown.Cert.freeEnergyLocalHolds_of.text: The result supplies a continuous periodic scalar enstrophy and its interval energy identity for free inverse outputs. Lemma II.3 additionally asserts continuity of an X-valued representative and applies to the full physical domain.

Breakdown.Cert.freeEquivariantHolds_of.text: The free inverse sends forcing invariant under every prescribed symmetry to a correction with the same symmetries. The proof uses equivariance of its heat-dilation gradient construction.

Breakdown.Cert.freeInv.text: The free inverse is the bounded operator selected by its gradient-integral characterisation; the existence and energy theorems justify its use for positive S.

Breakdown.Cert.freeInvHolds_of.text: The theorem constructs the free inverse in the spatial derivative representation and gives $\lVert\Delta v\rVert_H^2+\frac{1}{4}\lVert\nabla v\rVert_H^2\le\lVert f\rVert_H^2$. The complete physical bijection on $D_S$ uses separate equation and uniqueness arguments.

Breakdown.Cert.freePerturbationHolds_of.text: A physical representative of the free inverse satisfies the weak perturbation conditions and the solenoidal test equation with the original forcing. This supplies the physical equation needed by the inverse construction.

Breakdown.Cert.halfOrderGraph.text: The spatial derivative graph is completed in the two L² derivative norms. Its membership theorem verifies that this closure still satisfies the original Fourier multiplier relation.

Breakdown.Cert.localCompactnessHolds_of.text: From bounded forcing and periods in a compact positive interval, the theorem extracts locally Cauchy subsequences of both velocity and gradient. Proposition II.5 also identifies the limit as $T_S^{-1}f$ and concludes convergence of the whole sequence.

Breakdown.Cert.mem_halfOrderGraph_iff.text: Membership in the closed graph is equivalent to h(ξ)=2π|ξ|g(ξ). Thus completion has introduced no derivative pairs beyond the intended relation.

Breakdown.Cert.periodContinuityHolds_of.text: The theorem proves weak convergence of free inverse outputs in the two-derivative space as positive periods and weak forcing converge. Strong local convergence in Proposition II.5 needs the separate compactness theorem.

Breakdown.Cert.physToHH.text: A physical forcing field is projected onto divergence-free fields slice by slice and represented over period-one time.

Breakdown.Cert.productBoundHolds_of.text: The bilinear bound uses the same $c_w$, weighted first-factor norm and essential gradient supremum of the second factor. For a continuous $X$-valued representative, the essential and ordinary suprema agree.

Breakdown.Cert.productSubHolds_of.text: The quadratic difference expands into the two bilinear terms with factors u−u′ and u′, both for projected forcing and almost everywhere for physical products.

Breakdown.Cert.readingEnergyHolds_of.text: The theorem identifies physical weighted energy, Frobenius gradient energy and pin pairings with the corresponding spatial derivative-space quantities. Retaining a certificate parameter through smoothing requires these equalities to be applied within an additional construction.

Breakdown.Cert.readingExistsHolds_proof.text: Every element of the spatial derivative space has physical velocity, gradient and weak-Hessian representatives, with a period-integrated Hessian bound. This justifies translating the derivative-space construction into weak fields.

Breakdown.Cert.rowNormHolds.text: The theorem assumes orthonormal rows with separate nonnegative squared weights and proves their triangle and norm bounds. The paper uses unnormalised orthogonal rows; dividing each nonzero row by its norm and using that norm squared as its weight translates the two formulas.

Breakdown.Cert.sizeZ.text: After multiplier normalisation the joint norm is $\sqrt{\lVert v\rVert_w^2+|\beta|^2}$. Restoring the original multiplier gives the term $\omega^2|\beta|^2$.

Breakdown.Cert.sliceReadingHolds_of.text: The theorem supplies physical weak gradients and uniformly bounded velocity and gradient slices at every time. It does not by itself assert continuity of the X-valued curve or the shorter-period energy identity.

Breakdown.Cert.sliceSupBoundHolds_of.text: The theorem proves the product-form slice estimate $\lVert u\rVert_\infty^2\le (2\pi)^{-1}\lVert\nabla u\rVert_2\lVert\Delta u\rVert_2$. The weighted bound with $c_w$ follows from $2\sqrt{w^*}ab\le a^2+w^*b^2$.

Breakdown.Cert.solProj.text: The operator is the orthogonal projection onto the solenoidal Fourier subspace, corresponding to the spatial Leray projection.

Breakdown.Cert.supGrad.text: The quantity is the essential supremum over period-one time of the homogeneous gradient norm, with infinity allowed outside the held class.

Breakdown.Cert.testDenseHolds_proof.text: A projected periodic forcing field that annihilates every compact solenoidal space-time test is zero. This is the separation consequence of density used in the projection argument.

Breakdown.Cert.testPairingHolds_proof.text: The full-time physical pairing with a compact solenoidal test equals the one-period Hilbert pairing after periodising the test and projecting the field.

Breakdown.ExtendedCertificateData.text: The data specify approximate and reference fields, derivative representatives, force coefficients, pins, parameter constraints and candidate bounds. Their analytic validity is imposed by the certificate conditions.

Breakdown.ExtendedCertificateData.atProf.text: The reference is changed to Wᵃ, the reference gap and form shift become zero, and the coercive and row constants are rescaled by the absorbed loss 1−ϑ.

Breakdown.ExtendedCertificateData.defect.text: The residual is the approximate similarity equation formed from its weak Hessian, selected pressure contribution and actuator coefficients.

Breakdown.ExtendedCertificateData.params.text: The parameter set is the product of box constraints on J and a squared weighted-ball constraint on its complement, allowing zero radii.

Breakdown.ExtendedCertificateData.rows.text: The row measurement is the square root of a finite weighted sum of squared period pairings with normalised rows.

Breakdown.ExtendedCertificateData.target.text: The correction pin target is the full-profile target minus the pin value of the approximate profile.

Breakdown.ExtendedCertificateData.transf.text: The transfer loss is the scalar $\vartheta=(c_1+c_0)c_r$ used to absorb the reference convection error.

Breakdown.ExtendedCertificateData.withUn.text: Actuators and V are divided by ω, approximate force coefficients are multiplied by ω, and the multiplier weight becomes one. The parameter constraints, period, profile and pins are preserved.

Breakdown.FarField.DecayBounds.text: The decay conclusion includes second spatial derivatives of velocity and the pressure gradient with cubic decay. The paper’s basic profile assumptions require only velocity and first-gradient decay.

Breakdown.FarField.IsSmoothOrbitField.text: The conditions describe a smooth nonzero recurrent velocity-pressure pair with uniform derivatives, a vanishing tail and square-integrable pressure gradient. Equality with a specified mild orbit is a separate condition.

Breakdown.FarField.IsVelocityOf.text: The physical velocity equals the specified orbit almost everywhere in space at every time. This is the precise relation needed to transport a selected orbit through smoothing.

Breakdown.FarField.breakdownOnTorus_of_w.text: The conclusion is conditional torus breakdown. It does not retain Corollary II.18’s rates, selected period or local comparison with the same certificate profile.

Breakdown.FarField.farFieldDecay_holds.text: The formal proof derives decay from the backward Oseen integral equation using weighted estimates and a small-tail inverse. The account instead invokes Chae–Wolf and interior derivative estimates after checking their hypotheses.

Breakdown.FarField.integralEquationOfOrb.text: The theorem gives the backward Oseen integral equation for the same smooth representative of the specified mild orbit, with integration over every positive backward time lag.

Breakdown.FarField.periodicLerayProfileE.text: The public conclusion gives existential smooth-profile existence from existential weak-profile existence. It omits Proposition II.17’s identity with the specified input orbit and Theorem II.1’s selected parameter and correction bounds.

Breakdown.FarField.smoothFieldOfOrbit_ho.text: The construction returns smooth velocity and pressure representing a given mild orbit at every time. It uses Fourier Sobolev and Picard estimates, while the written account applies the bounded-mild regularity theorem.

Breakdown.Freq.X.text: The formal homogeneous space consists of solenoidal first-derivative Fourier symbols. Identifying it with the paper’s canonical divergence-free L⁶ velocity requires the physical representation and Sobolev results.

Breakdown.Held.convexCompactFixedPoint.text: Every continuous self-map of a nonempty compact convex set in finite dimension has a fixed point. No assumption of nonempty interior is imposed.

Breakdown.Held.testSetZero_of.text: The coordinate bounds make the raw update a continuous self-map of K. Its fixed point gives VᵀΦ=0, and invertibility of V gives exact zero force.

Breakdown.IsExtendedCertificate.text: The formal certificate adds global joint C¹ regularity, a weak Hessian with cubic decay, symmetry of the weight, c₂≥0 and a uniform spatial L² bound on each adjoint slice. It also permits m=1 when the paper would select an available half-period symmetry.

Breakdown.IsPerturbation.text: The domain specifies weak gradient and Hessian representatives and the square-integrable combined time-and-dilation derivative. The paper writes $D_S$ through distributional derivatives of the velocity; a physical representation argument relates the two.

Breakdown.IsRightSide.text: The linear perturbation equation is tested against compact smooth solenoidal fields, with the Laplacian integrated by parts. This expresses equality of the right side modulo gradients.

Breakdown.PeriodicSimilarityProfileExist.text: The smooth-profile existence condition contains recurrence and decay but no certificate parameter or correction. The additional recurrence in Remark II.19 requires the separately retained symmetry of the same velocity.

Breakdown.Space.text: The spatial variable belongs to Euclidean three-space with its Euclidean inner product and norm.

Breakdown.Symmetry.text: Each prescribed symmetry consists of an orthogonal spatial map paired with a real time shift.

Breakdown.WeakProfile.weakOrbitOfParts_h.text: The construction produces a continuous mild orbit from measurable weak-profile data after the required weak-derivative and representative results are supplied. Its existential conclusion does not retain the selected certificate parameter or identify a specified input field at every time.

Breakdown.exists_fixedPoint_box.text: A continuous self-map of a closed finite-dimensional box has a fixed point, including degenerate boxes. Zero force still requires the separate proof that the raw update maps K into itself.

Breakdown.extended_certificate_breakdown.text: The conclusion is whole-space breakdown from an extended certificate. It does not retain the displayed blow-up rate, quantitative approximation or selected certificate profile.

Breakdown.extended_certificate_orbit_pro.text: The theorem gives existential weak-profile existence from an extended certificate. It omits the chosen parameter, its period identity, the actual correction, the joint multiplier bound, pins and every-time symmetry conclusions.

Breakdown.matSq.text: The squared Frobenius gradient norm is the sum of the squared lengths of its three columns.

Breakdown.periodLIntegral.text: The quantity is the nonnegative integral over one period and all of space; it may be infinite until integrability is proved.

Breakdown.periodNorm.text: For a periodic square-integrable field, the quantity is its H norm obtained from the squared integral over one period.

Breakdown.pinValue.text: The pin functional integrates the Frobenius pairing of the gradient with the prescribed matrix field over one period and all space.

Breakdown.stationaryEnergy.text: The single-slice energy is the squared Laplacian norm plus the spatially weighted squared Frobenius gradient norm.

Breakdown.supBoundFactor.text: The constant is $c_w=1/\sqrt{4\pi\sqrt{w^*}}$, agreeing algebraically with the weighted product estimate.

Breakdown.weightedEnergy.text: The weighted energy integrates |Δv|²+w|∇v|F² over one period. Its interpretation as a real energy requires the derivative integrals to be finite.

topics.name: The blow-up statements
topics.description: Smooth solutions, breakdown on space and on the torus, and the theorems that state them (Theorem 1.1, Theorem 7.1).

topics.name: The fractional extension
topics.description: The authors' separate extension with dissipation exponent between 1 and 5/4, outside the classical paper.

topics.name: Heat flow and mild solutions
topics.description: The heat semigroup, the bilinear Duhamel term, mild solutions, restarting and uniqueness (§3).

topics.name: Recurrent profiles
topics.description: Self-similar time-periodic profiles, their slices and orbits, and weak profiles read as physical fields (§2, §4.1, §7.11).

topics.name: Monodromy and the correction
topics.description: The period map, its compact-plus-small splitting, the spectral projection and the fixed point that corrects a profile to an exact solution (§4).

topics.name: Passing to the torus
topics.description: The solenoidal cutoff, periodization and the periodic right inverse that move the construction onto the torus (§5–6).

topics.name: From certificate to profile
topics.description: Certificate data, the free operator, convection, held solutions and the smoothing of the weak profile they produce (§7).

topics.name: The coercive multiplier estimate
topics.description: The multiplier, its five density coefficients and lower bound, and the a priori estimate it gives (Appendix B.1 and B.2).

topics.name: Encoded cell data
topics.description: The finitely represented inputs: coordinates and harmonics, the profile representation, splines and jets, physical cells, rows, weights and potentials.

topics.name: Reduction to the quarter plane
topics.description: Symmetry reduction of the density to the meridian quarter plane (B.3).

topics.name: Cells, traces and tails
topics.description: Integrability, the common vector of unknowns, resolved modes, the tail budget and the exterior estimate (B.4).

topics.name: Angular and ray-exterior tests
topics.description: The angular inequalities, the pointwise test and the integrated test on ray exteriors (B.5 and B.6).

topics.name: The matrix tree lower bound
topics.description: The tree conditions on the cell matrices and the passage from all cells to the global inequality (B.7 and B.8).

topics.name: Changing the profile
topics.description: Bounds for moving estimates from the reference field to the actual profile (B.9).

topics.name: The adjoint pairing and its error
topics.description: The quadratic adjoint pairing, the azimuthal dual norm and the linear adjoint error with potentials and pins (B.10 to B.12).

topics.name: The offset and the certificate
topics.description: Enclosing the constant, linear and quadratic offset, and the fifteen fields of CellSystemCondition that make the data a certificate (B.13 and B.14).
